differences.what: massing: a two-storey brick block over a raised stone basement under a mansard, the street front and the south flank both seen, the corner at x 588 px
differences.how: T-2963: the 1911 sheet's 14.82 x 12.0 m front block on K01, two storeys (4.8 and 5.3 m) over a 2.0 m basement; the render's corner stands on x 588

differences.what: the basement in pale ashlar in level courses from grade to a projecting water table at the principal floor, round the street front, both canted bays and the south flank, with barred lights under the bays' windows; built as brick to grade
differences.how: T-1886: K01's stone front stopped at the principal floor (stone_front.brick_above_m 2.0) under a 0.28 m coping, carried round the south flank (side_base) and through both bays (front_stone, brick over a 2.0 m basement storey) with a barred light in each face the camera sees; the render's stone stands from grade to the brick at the print's line and its lights under the print's, offset with the bays by the 1 m above

differences.what: the basement's coursing: about six level joints a third of a metre apart in the print; the render's smooth limestone shows three base courses to the lights' heads and plain ashlar over them
differences.how: T-1886: joints under 0.02 m wide in a stone of the right extent, tone and dressing; the profile lays the rusticated base to the lights' heads (L-k01-1816-henderson-1886)

differences.what: the canted bay at the street front's south corner, two storeys of windows in its faces, the cornice carried round it
differences.how: T-2963: a K08 canted bay 6.87 m at the wall and 1.65 m out (the sheet's), carrying K10's bed moulding and the eave round its plan (eaves.cornice)

differences.what: the canted bay on the south flank near its rear, a window in each face
differences.how: T-2963: a K08 canted bay 4.85 m at the wall and 1.0 m out (the sheet's)

differences.what: the porch: turned columns at the landing's front corners, an entablature over them and an iron balcony railing on it, the flight straight down to the walk
differences.how: T-2963: K01's door hood standing on two turned columns over plinths with responds at the wall (hood.columns), 2.0 m out and 3.0 m wide, its railing in iron

differences.what: the bracketed cornice and the slated mansard with dormers in its street and south faces
differences.how: T-2963: K10's bracketed timber cornice and K05's mansard 4.0 m over the eave, two street dormers and one south

differences.what: an iron fence on a stone curb along the street line with a gate at the stoop's foot
differences.how: T-2963: K11's spear fence on its curb 7.4 m before the front

differences.what: the porch and the front's canted bay stand about 1 m further south in the print than on the 1911 trace (the porch's columns read 60-75 px right of the print's through this camera)
differences.how: T-2964: the 1911 sheet's trace and this photograph's camera fit disagree about it, and no third source places the porch; under the T-3153 bar a gap two sources or two fits disagree about is within tolerance. The trace keeps the porch where the sheet draws it.

differences.what: the raised mansard crown over the front's south end, with its own curb and iron cresting, standing higher than the main roof
differences.how: T-2964: the front's canted bay carried up through the cornice into a mansard of its own (K08's roof.mansard): 4.4 m of lower face at 76 degrees over the bay's eaves, its deck 0.4 m over the main curb, K10's iron cresting 0.6 m high round its curb. Its rise is read as a fraction of the corner's height through this camera (about a third), good to about half a metre

differences.what: the south flank's bay carried up through the cornice under its own mansard, and its cresting; built stopping under the cornice with a low hip
differences.how: T-2964: the flank bay's upper storey raised to the wall head (5.04 m, as the front bay's), the bracketed cornice run round it (K10, now on any wall), and over it a K08 mansard 4.0 m at 76 degrees under iron cresting; its rise reads about two-fifths of the wall under it in both the print and the render

differences.what: the dormers in the two crowns' own faces: one on the front crown's street face, one on the flank crown's south face
differences.how: T-1886: one pedimented dormer on each crown's front face (K08 mansard_dormers, the main dormers' 40-degree gabled head, a 0.7 by 1.4 m sash); through the camera they render where the print's stand, the front crown's about 1 m north of the print's with the porch and bay (the within-tolerance item above)

differences.what: the flank crown's second dormer, in its south-east canted face (x 230-290 px)
differences.how: T-1886: K08 lays a bay's mansard dormers on its front face only; a dormer on a canted face is a kit change (L-k01-1816-henderson-1886)

differences.what: both crowns' lower faces slated as the main mansard, the print drawing all three alike; built in a plain grey sheet
differences.how: T-1886: the crowns roof.slated_as_house (T-1881), so they take the main mansard's own slate

differences.what: iron cresting along every roof deck
differences.how: T-2964: K10's iron cresting along the main deck's street curb (mansard.deck.cresting, as 1801's) and round both crowns' curbs; the main deck's south curb shows none in the print behind the flank crown, and its north and rear curbs are out of this camera's sight. The pattern is the kit's (the print's panels read only as a dense pierced band)

differences.what: the dormers pedimented with carved cheeks; built round-headed
differences.how: T-2964: all three main dormers square-headed under a 40-degree pediment (K01's gabled dormer head, T-2452)

differences.what: the dormers' carved cheeks
differences.how: T-2964: carving under a foot deep on a dormer 1.1 m wide; the dormers' size, place and pediment are built

differences.what: the window hoods carved, with a scrolled crest over each, on the flat front's windows; built as K09's plain cornice-hood lintels
differences.how: T-1886: K09's carved crest (street_front_trim.crest, T-3270's palmette between two volutes, 1.0 m wide and 0.35 m high) stands on every cornice hood of both storeys; through the camera each renders over its hood where the print's raised crest stands

differences.what: the south flank's window under the front's crested hood, its consoles hanging past the jambs (x 350-385 px); built under a K03 brick segmental arch
differences.how: T-1886: the flank window named in street_front_trim.lights on both storeys, so it wears its storey's K09 hood and crest in the brick (K01 now lets a brick side wall's named light take its K09 head)

differences.what: the crested hoods over the two canted bays' windows (x 140-215 and 490-560 px); built with K08's own plain hoods
differences.how: T-1886: K08 dresses a bay's windows with its own hood and does not read street_front_trim's crest; a crest on a K08 hood is a kit change (L-k01-1816-henderson-1886)

differences.what: the porch columns' carved capitals
differences.how: T-2964: the columns, their plinths and the square capital blocks stand where the print's do; the carving is under the bar

differences.what: the balcony's railing about 1 m high with pierced iron panels, and the window over the door opening onto it as a door; built as a 0.6 m railing of square balusters in front of a window
differences.how: T-2964 tried the railing at 0.95 m: K01's door hood then runs into the sill of the window over the door (7.5 m), so the two are one change — that window made a door to the balcony floor, which K01 does not yet build

differences.what: the fence's scrolled cast-iron panels and its tall posts; built as the kit's spears
differences.how: T-2964: K11's scroll-band fence on its curb, the nearest panel K11 has to the print's scrollwork

differences.what: the fence panels' pattern: scrollwork the fence's full height in the print, a band of scrolls under the top rail in the kit
differences.how: T-2964: a pattern inside a fence of the right height, kind and line

differences.what: the brick's tone: dark in the print on the street front and the south flank alike; built red on the front and the bays (T-3385's pressed red) and buff on the flank between them
differences.how: T-1886: the south flank between the bays laid in the front's pressed red (face_brick.returns ['south'], a K01 key new here), with no brick string course on it, as the print draws none; through the camera the flank, the bays and the front now render one brick, as the print's median greys do (flank 169-184, bays 174-200). The red's depth against the print's grey is the palette's (T-3385)

differences.what: the tall chimney stack behind the front's south end
differences.how: T-2964: read through the rebuilt render, the stack stands between the flank crown and the front crown with its head over the crown's cresting, as the print's does, about 35 px (under a metre) east of it
